title: Definition of a concept
description: A machine-written definition of one concept (the review response, F06; ADR-0136). Its own record rather than a field on the concept, because a signed concept cannot be edited and approving a label approves no definition (ADR-0071's reason for a concept's kind). Every definition carries the authoring envelope, quoting the passages it rests on, and says where its words come from. One per concept per scope (1.1.0, ADR-0147): a concept with several definitions carries a distinct `scope` on each.

concept.description: The concept defined, signed or machine-written. It must exist in one of the two stores.

text.description: The definition. For a statutory_definition, the instrument's own words, verbatim; otherwise the author's wording, staying within the quoted evidence.

basis.description: Where the words come from. statutory_definition: the Act's or Regulations' own definition, quoted (preferred, CHAT-0045). statutory_provision: written from a provision that says what the thing is or does. manual: written from the Manual, which states practice, not law (CLAUDE.md rule 5).

scope_note.description: Which sense of a word the definition is of, where the corpus uses it in several ("application" first, the 8 October review's B2), or which Part of the Regulations a definition belongs to.

scope.description: A machine-readable key for the context this definition holds in, where a concept has more than one (1.1.0, ADR-0147): a Part of an instrument (`TMR1995/Part17`), a sense (`sense:application-document`), or a period (`period:2026-09-19/`). Required on every definition of a concept that has several, no two alike; a reader picks one only when its context names the scope, and otherwise reports the concept unresolved. Absent on a concept's only definition. scope_note stays the words a reader sees.

source_ref.description: The passage the definition is principally drawn from; one of the evidence refs.
